newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up against the U.S. dollar on Monday at 8.2964 from Friday's 8.2970 on market expectations that China would announce a solid foreign trade surplus for March, traders said.
The weighted average price on Friday was 8.2969.
The yuan opened higher at 8.2960 and hit an intraday high of 8.2950 early in the session. It then consolidated and moved around 8.2965 until the close, hitting a low of 8.2968.
Dealers said the yuan gained strong support at about 8.2965 mainly due to expectations on the March surplus. China's foreign trade surplus for January and February was $3.8 billion.

"The date for announcing the previous month's trade figures is approaching and most traders expect the surplus for March to be big," said a dealer. "The heavy trade surplus has been a major factor supporting the yuan in the past few months."
China usually announces foreign trade data for the previous month at about mid-month.
Business was slow in early trading on Monday, but later became more active with sentiment good, traders said.
"Buying emerged soon after trading began because of the good sentiment, and that dominated the market for the rest of the session," a second dealer said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to move up slightly on Tuesday.
The yuan closed down at 6.5721 from 6.5600 against 100 Japanese yen and almost unchanged at 1.0715 from 1.0717 against the Hong Kong dollar.
